about.title: Ione Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Ione is a small town, but its roads still see real traffic pressure, particularly where Rt 104, Preston Avenue, Shakeley Lane, and W Main Street funnel commuters and through-traffic. Recent public records show 10 injury collisions and 14 people injured in a single year here, with reported crashes clustering on Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. — a pattern worth knowing if your case involves a dispute over how a crash happened. When someone is injured in a collision on these corridors, the insurance process that follows can feel just as disorienting as the crash itself. We handle personal injury claims directly, evaluate your case, manage communication with insurers, and explain what California law allows. There's no cost for an initial consultation, and we work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there's a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Talking to the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: You generally have two years to file a car accident claim in California, but if a government entity or road condition is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Acting early preserves your options.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning an insurer may try to shift partial blame onto you to reduce what they owe. We can push back on unfair fault allocations before they become part of the official record.

items.title: Recorded Statements Can Be Used Against You
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often ask for a recorded statement soon after a crash, but anything you say can later be used to minimize your claim. It's worth speaking with us first, especially since California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Ione?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. If a government-maintained road or vehicle was involved, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's best to get advice sooner rather than later.

items.question: Does it matter that my crash happened on a road like Rt 104 or Shakeley Lane?
items.answer: The specific road doesn't change your legal rights, but documenting exactly where and how the crash happened — including any road conditions — can matter for building your claim. We can help gather that evidence while it's still available.

items.question: Will I owe anything to speak with an attorney?
items.answer: No. Our initial consultation is free, and we work on contingency, which means we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost or obligation to move forward.
